Never buy these chocolate brands again.  Kinder, Kit Kat, Lindt, Snickers, M&Ms, Hersheys and Cadbury All of the chocolate brands I just showed you have one thing in common. They are all starting to use lab-grown chocolate.  They are spending billions of dollars into biotech startups that are making the switch from real cocoa to lab-grown.  It's made by extracting cacao cells, multiplying them in massive steel bioreactors, and then processing it into fake chocolate. How to make Chocolate!—it’s not that hard! Making chocolate is a delicious process that starts from a simple bean and ends with the sweet treat we all love. Let’s walk through how it’s made, step by step. It all begins with cocoa beans, which grow inside large pods on cacao trees. Farmers harvest the pods, crack them open, and remove the beans. These beans are then fermented and dried in the sun, which helps develop their flavor. Once dried, the beans are roasted. Roasting brings out the rich, chocolatey aroma and taste. After roasting, the outer shells of the beans are removed, leaving behind the cocoa nibs—the part we actually use to make chocolate. The nibs are ground into a thick, gritty paste called chocolate liquor. Don’t be fooled by the name—there’s no alcohol in it. This paste is made up of cocoa solids and cocoa butter. To turn it into smooth, sweet chocolate, sugar is added. If you want milk chocolate, milk powder or condensed milk is mixed in too. Then everything is blended and refined until the texture becomes silky and smooth. After that, the mixture is tempered, which means it’s carefully heated and cooled to give the chocolate a shiny finish and a nice snap when you break it. Finally, the chocolate is poured into molds, shaped into bars or fun figures, and left to cool and harden. And just like that, the journey from bean to bar is complete. Now all that’s left to do is unwrap it and take a bite. Enjoy!
